# Redacted billing fixtures

The JSON fixture contains `periodStartDate` and `periodEndDate` (inclusive ISO local dates), printed `importPeakKwh`, `importOffpeakKwh`, and `exportKwh` (non-negative kWh strings), `lines` (`{code,amount}` in MYR), `total` (MYR), and `openingLots` / `closingLots` (`{originStart,kwh}`). Optional `importByMonth` contains `{month:"YYYY-MM",kwh}` entries reconstructed from the ledger; optional `importByWindow` and `exportByWindow` contain `{window,kwh}` entries reconstructed from measured bucket data. Month imports must sum to printed total import; window imports must separately match printed peak (all non-default windows) and off-peak (the default window); window exports must sum to printed total export, within 0.001 kWh. A contradictory split is refused rather than overriding the printed bill. Names, addresses, meter IDs and account numbers must never be copied into a fixture; strict validation rejects unknown fields.

The optional top-level `synthetic: true` marker identifies harness-only data (the JSON examples use it). The schema accepts this boolean, but `reproduceBill` ignores it; it does not make a tariff bill-verified or supply any missing billing quantities.

The verifier refuses (`ok:false`, with `refusals`) rather than fabricating missing distributions: a bill spanning calendar months with a monthly component requires `importByMonth`, and a multi-window NEM bill with export requires `exportByWindow`. A single-month bill needs no month split. The printed ToU import split is sufficient for one declared peak window plus the default window; additional windows require `importByWindow`. A refusal cannot mark a tariff version bill-verified. The entered holiday table must match the utility's applied holidays. Synthetic fixtures below contain invented rates and quantities only. A real redacted bill must reproduce every printed line and total within RM 0.01 before a tariff version is marked bill-verified.
